newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 9.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The army will buy armoured vehicles that meet the needs of the Second Infantry Division most, says army commander-in-chief. He says the army will make a decision on the purchase of armoured vehicles after considering the results of tactical and mobility tests on nine models, prices and comments from the division. (BANGKOK POST)

- Police chief Pracha Promnok says the standoff between Central Investigation Bureau Deputy Commissioner Seri Temiyavej and Metropolitan Police Bureau Commissioner Sophon Waratchanon over a crackdown on illegal bookmaking at Bangkok's two major horse racetracks is triggered by a misunderstanding. The standoff comes to a head when Seri accuses the Metropolitan Police Bureau of corruption and of failing to crack down on illegal bookmaking activities at the Royal Turf Club and the Royal Sports Club. (THE NATION)

- Two Judicial officials facing a disciplinary probe on suspicion of taking bribes from suspected drug trafficker Li Yun Chung have reported to the investigation panel to hear accusations against them. Region 1 Court chief justice says he has not proposed transfer of the two judges because so far they have only been suspected of involvement. (BANGKOK POST)

- SkyBridge, a subsidiary of Alcatel Alsthom which is active in satellite based broadband transmission, is planning to penetrate into the market of satellite transmission in KU band despite the fact that this frequency spectrum is almost fully occupied. The company, which is planning to operate a satellite link transmission network worldwide under the trade name of "SkyBridge", is now on a roadshow in search for local partners, in designated countries including Thailand, to operate gateways. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Bank of Thailand will exercise its power to force mergers of the 16 suspended finance companies if they fail to submit their merger plans by the deadline on Friday. So far the only plan for a merger involving any of the 16 has come from Nava Finance and Securities Plc, which has indicated that will absorb CMIC Finance and Securities Plc and one other collapsed company. (THE NATION)
